scope.name: released single-camera subset
scope.note: These are subset reproducibility numbers. The paper's headline full-deployment values must remain separate and are not reproduced here.

track_proxy.method: greedy visual-only cosine on normalized SigLIP 768-d + max gap 3 s + max duration 60 s + max size 20
track_proxy.selected_rule: strictest threshold within 5% of best calibration objective

motion_energy.definition: mean absolute grayscale difference between consecutive released snapshots (96x96), averaged per clip

cannot_reproduce: semantic running/fighting labels beyond the released VLM captions
notes: All labels are derived from released metadata; none are human annotations.
Action queries use VLM caption event labels (fighting/smoke) and a motion-energy proxy; no running/fighting label is invented.
Track queries use single-camera colour-continuity proxies; cross-camera tracking is untestable.

retrieval.semantic_aggregation: max over frames per clip for the main table; mean reported as sensitivity
retrieval.structured_branch: metadata-only score: time overlap, camera, VLM zone, person colour/attributes, caption count mode, caption event, motion-energy proxy

minmax.comparison: adaptive vs fixed_0.7 (fixed alpha selected on tune split)

zscore.comparison: adaptive vs fixed_1.0 (fixed alpha selected on tune split)

count_estimate.definition: window mode of released caption person counts vs anchor-frame count

limitations: PROTOCOL NOTE: this raw benchmark is a code-path smoke test, not the benchmark quoted in the paper. It is not protocol-matched to the deployment C1 study: count questions are free 'how many' questions with no target count (so the structured branch has no numeric target to rank on) and action queries carry explicit time windows (so the structured branch has a time cue that the action override suppresses). The number quoted in the paper comes from the protocol-matched control, backend/scripts/eval_retrieval_control.py (results/retrieval_control_tables.md).
Single camera (camera_0) and a 2-hour released window; cross-camera retrieval and identity tracking are untestable.
Labels are derived from released VLM captions, detector metadata and snapshots, not human annotations; no IAA is available.
Two clips on disk are not in the scene FAISS index (121 indexed of 123); evaluation uses the indexed clips.
Action queries use 15 weak VLM caption events (fighting/smoke) plus 15 motion-energy proxy queries; no running/fighting labels are invented.
Track queries are single-camera colour-continuity proxies, not ground-truth identities.
The full-deployment 0.666->0.828 / 0.785->0.807 values are not reproduced and must not be replaced by these subset numbers.
